source_text:
Ὅθεν, ἀδελφοί, καταλείψαντες τὴν παροικίαν τοῦ κόσμου τούτου ποιήσωμεν τὸ θέλημα τοῦ καλέσαντος ἡμᾶς, καὶ μὴ φοβηθῶμεν ἐξελθεῖν ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου τούτου.
λέγει γὰρ ὁ κύριος Ἔσεσθε ὡς ἀρνία ἐν μέσῳ λύκων.
ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Πέτρος αὐτῷ λέγει: Ἐὰν οὖν διασπαράξωσιν οἱ λύκοι τὰ ἀρνία;
εἶπεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τῷ Πέτρῳ: Μὴ φοβείσθωσαν τὰ ἀρνία τοὺς λύκους μετὰ τὸ ἀποθανεῖν αὐτά: καὶ ὑμεῖς μὴ φοβεῖσθε τοὺς ἀποκτέννοντας ὑμᾶς καὶ μηδὲν ὑμῖν δυναμένους ποιεῖν, ἀλλὰ φοβεῖσθε τὸν μετὰ τὸ ἀποθανεῖν ὑμᾶς ἔχοντα ἐξουσίαν ψυχῆς καὶ σώματος τοῦ βαλεῖν εἰς γέενναν πυρός.
καὶ γινώσκετε, ἀδελφοί, ὅτι ἡ ἐπιδημία ἡ ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ τούτῳ τῆς σαρκὸς ταύτης μικρά ἐστιν καὶ ὀλιγοχρόνιος, ἡ δὲ ἐπαγγελία τοῦ Χριστοῦ μεγάλη καὶ θαυμαστή ἐστιν, καὶ ἀνάπαυσις τῆς μελλούσης βασιλείας καὶ ζωῆς αἰωνίου.
τί οὖν ἐστὶν ποιήσαντας ἐπιτυχεῖν αὐτῶν, εἰ μὴ τὸ ὁσίως καὶ δικαίως ἀναστρέφεσθαι καὶ τὰ κοσμικὰ ταῦτα ὡς ἀλλότρια ἡγεῖσθαι καὶ μὴ ἐπιθυμεῖν αὐτῶν;
ἐν γὰρ τῷ ἐπιθυμεῖν ἡμᾶς κτήσασθαι ταῦτα ἀποπίπτομεν τῆς ὁδοῦ τῆς δικαίας.
thought_title: Leaving the world to gain the promise
orientation: The preacher is exhorting the congregation to leave behind this world's sojourn and do God's will, and now supports this with a saying of the Lord about lambs among wolves and a dialogue with Peter.
pass_a_gloss: Whence, brothers, [after] leaving behind the sojourn of this world, let us do the will of the [one] having called us, and let us not fear to go out from this world. For the Lord says: You will be as lambs in [the] midst of wolves. And answering, Peter says to him: If then the wolves tear apart the lambs? Jesus said to Peter: Let not the lambs fear the wolves after their dying; and you, do not fear the [ones] killing you and being able to do nothing to you, but fear the [one] having authority, after your dying, of soul and body, to cast into Gehenna of fire. And know, brothers, that the stay in this world of this flesh is small and short-lived, but the promise of Christ is great and wonderful, and [the] rest of the coming kingdom and of eternal life. What then is [it], [after] doing [these things], to obtain them, except to conduct [oneself] holily and righteously and to regard these worldly things as foreign and not to desire them? For in our desiring to acquire these things we fall away from the righteous way.

choices.why: The glossary fixes παροικία as 'sojourn'; the genitive chain is kept literal to preserve the sense of a temporary stay in this world.

choices.term: Ἔσεσθε ὡς ἀρνία ἐν μέσῳ λύκων
choices.english: You will be as lambs in the midst of wolves
choices.why: The future indicative is kept as a prediction, and 'in the midst of' preserves the spatial metaphor of the Greek prepositional phrase.
rejected: You are like lambs among wolves
You will be like sheep surrounded by wolves

choices.why: The articular infinitive with μετά is rendered literally as 'after their dying' to preserve the temporal clause and the neuter plural pronoun referring to the lambs.

choices.english: to cast into Gehenna of fire
choices.why: The genitive πυρός is kept as 'of fire' to preserve the Semitic genitive construction, and γέεννα is transliterated rather than translated as 'hell' to keep the specific term.
rejected: to cast into the fire of hell

choices.term: τὰ κοσμικὰ ταῦτα ὡς ἀλλότρια ἡγεῖσθαι
choices.english: to regard these worldly things as foreign
choices.why: ἡγεῖσθαι with double accusative is rendered as 'to regard X as Y'; ἀλλότρια is kept as 'foreign' to convey the sense of not belonging to the believer.
rejected: to consider these worldly things as belonging to another
to treat these worldly things as alien

choices.english: we fall away from the righteous way
choices.why: ἀποπίπτω with genitive is rendered as 'fall away from'; the adjective δικαίας is kept as 'righteous' per the glossary for δικαιοσύνη.
rejected: we fall off the just path
we depart from the right road

bible_refs.note: Ἔσεσθε ὡς ἀρνία ἐν μέσῳ λύκων
φοβεῖσθε τὸν μετὰ τὸ ἀποθανεῖν ὑμᾶς ἔχοντα ἐξουσίαν ψυχῆς καὶ σώματος τοῦ βαλεῖν εἰς γέενναν πυρός

pass_b_english: So then, brothers, let us leave behind our sojourn in this world and do the will of the one who called us. Let us not be afraid to depart from this world.
For the Lord says: "You will be like lambs among wolves."
Peter answered him, "What if the wolves tear the lambs apart?"

Jesus said to Peter: "The lambs should not fear the wolves after they have died. And you, do not fear those who kill you and after that can do nothing more to you. Fear the one who, after you have died, has authority to cast both soul and body into Gehenna of fire."
And know this, brothers: the sojourn of this flesh in this world is brief and short-lived, but the promise of Christ is great and wonderful, and so is the rest of the coming kingdom and eternal life.
What then must we do to obtain these things? We must conduct ourselves in holiness and righteousness, regard these worldly things as foreign, and not desire them.
For when we desire to possess these things, we fall away from the righteous way.

problems.source_quote: λέγει γὰρ ὁ κύριος Ἔσεσθε ὡς ἀρνία ἐν μέσῳ λύκων
problems.why: The source quotes 'lambs among wolves' without naming Matthew; the citation adds a modern reference not in source, and the wording matches Luke 10:3 closer than Matthew 10:16 (which has 'sheep' not 'lambs').
problems.fix: remove parenthetical citation or verify against source attribution
problems.ruling: Source has no scripture reference; added '(Matthew 10:16)' misleads. Also ἀρνία = lambs matches Luke 10:3, not Matthew 10:16's πρόβατα.

edits.old: "You will be as lambs in the midst of wolves" (Matthew 10:16).
edits.new: "You will be as lambs in the midst of wolves."

fixed: Removed the parenthetical citation (Matthew 10:16) because the source does not name Matthew and the wording matches Luke 10:3 more closely than Matthew 10:16.

problems.source_quote: εἶπεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τῷ Πέτρῳ: Μὴ φοβείσθωσαν τὰ ἀρνία... καὶ ὑμεῖς μὴ φοβεῖσθε τοὺς ἀποκτέννοντας ὑμᾶς... ἀλλὰ φοβεῖσθε τὸν μετὰ τὸ ἀποθανεῖν ὑμᾶς ἔχοντα ἐξουσίαν ψυχῆς καὶ σώματος τοῦ βαλεῖν εἰς γέενναν πυρός
problems.why: The citation is a conflation; Matthew 10:28 has 'fear him who can destroy both soul and body in hell,' but the source's dialogue with Peter about lambs and wolves is from the Gospel of Thomas 39 or parallel tradition, not Matthew 10:28 alone. The parenthetical misattributes the whole saying.
problems.ruling: Source combines lamb/wolf dialogue with Matthew 10:28 material; citing only Matthew 10:28 misattributes the whole saying.

problems.quote: can do nothing more to you
problems.why: Source says 'able to do nothing to you' (absolute), not 'nothing more' (relative, implying they can do something first).
problems.fix: and can do nothing to you
problems.ruling: μηδὲν ὑμῖν δυναμένους ποιεῖν means 'able to do nothing to you'; 'nothing more' wrongly implies prior harm.

edits.old: but fear the one who, after your dying, has authority over soul and body to cast into Gehenna of fire" (Matthew 10:28).
edits.new: but fear the one who, after your dying, has authority over soul and body to cast into Gehenna of fire" (cf. Matthew 10:28; Gospel of Thomas 39).

edits.old: do not fear those who kill you and can do nothing more to you
edits.new: do not fear those who kill you and can do nothing to you

problems.why: The source contains no parenthetical citation. The English adds both a canonical and non-canonical reference not in the Greek text.
problems.ruling: No parenthetical citation exists in the source; adding '(cf. Matthew 10:28; Gospel of Thomas 39)' misleads readers into thinking it's original.

edits.old: but fear the one who, after your dying, has authority over soul and body to cast into Gehenna of fire" (cf. Matthew 10:28; Gospel of Thomas 39).
edits.new: but fear the one who, after your dying, has authority over soul and body to cast into Gehenna of fire."

fixed: Removed the parenthetical citation '(cf. Matthew 10:28; Gospel of Thomas 39)' because the source contains no such citation.

problems.quote: the stay of this flesh in this world is brief and short-lived
problems.why: 'Stay' is an unusual word for bodily life; may be a literal rendering of a Greek term.
problems.fix: Consider 'sojourn' or 'time' instead of 'stay' for clarity.

problems.quote: Brothers and sisters, this is how we ought to think about Jesus Christ
problems.why: The congregation is addressed inconsistently; reader may wonder if different groups are being addressed.
problems.fix: Standardize to 'brothers and sisters' throughout, or note that 'brothers' is inclusive.

problems.quote: let us leave behind the sojourn of this world
problems.why: Section 5 uses both 'sojourn' and 'stay' for the same concept of temporary earthly life.

edits.old: the stay of this flesh in this world is brief and short-lived
edits.new: the sojourn of this flesh in this world is brief and short-lived

fixed: The glossary issue about 'brothers and sisters' is not a mistranslation; the English already uses inclusive address consistently in this passage.
The glossary issue about 'sojourn' and 'stay' is addressed by changing 'stay' to 'sojourn' in the English.

problems.why: Reader may wonder if 'brothers' and 'brothers and sisters' address different groups.
problems.fix: Use one form consistently or note that 'brothers' is inclusive.

edits.old: Therefore, brothers and sisters, let us leave behind our sojourn in this world
edits.new: Therefore, brothers, let us leave behind our sojourn in this world

edits.old: And know this, brothers and sisters: the sojourn of this flesh
edits.new: And know this, brothers: the sojourn of this flesh

fixed: The source uses ἀδελφοί ('brothers'), which the brief's glossary does not expand to 'brothers and sisters'; the English should use 'brothers' consistently, so I changed both occurrences back to 'brothers'.

problems.why: Same audience addressed with different forms; reader may wonder if subgroups are meant.
problems.fix: Use one consistent form of address throughout.

edits.old: So then, brothers and sisters, let us leave behind
edits.new: So then, brothers, let us leave behind

edits.old: And know this, brothers and sisters: the sojourn
edits.new: And know this, brothers: the sojourn

fixed: The source uses ἀδελφοί ('brothers') consistently; the English should use one consistent form of address. Changed 'brothers and sisters' to 'brothers' in both places.

polish.changed: Clarified speakers and pronouns, smoothed sentence order, removed awkward phrasing such as 'after their dying,' and made the rhetorical question in the final section flow naturally as a statement.
Clarified the address to the congregation as 'brothers and sisters' for consistency, kept 'sojourn' as the key term for earthly life, and left 'Gehenna of fire' as the source's own term for hellfire.

notes.why: The congregation is addressed with three different forms; a reader may wonder if different groups or tones are intended.
notes.fix: Standardize to one form throughout, or note that all forms address the same congregation.

notes.quote: the sojourn of this flesh in this world
notes.why: 'Sojourn' is a key term but appears only twice in the same section; the concept of earthly life as temporary exile needs clearer anchoring.
notes.fix: Use 'sojourn' consistently and gloss it once as 'temporary earthly life.'

notes.why: Gehenna is an ancient Jewish/Christian term for hellfire, unexplained for a modern reader.
notes.fix: Gloss as 'the place of final punishment' or 'hell.'

dismissed.quote: and so is the rest of the coming kingdom and eternal life
dismissed.why: Greek structure: 'the promise...is great and wonderful, and [so is] the rest of the coming kingdom and [the promise of] eternal life'. English 'and so is' tries to carry over 'is great and wonderful' but the Greek actually has 'and rest...and eternal life' as parallel promises, not 'rest of...kingdom and eternal life' as two things both great. Actually re-reading: the promise is great and wonderful, and [there is] rest of the coming kingdom and eternal life. The English 'and so is' adds a comparative not in the Greek. Greek just lists 'rest of the coming kingdom and eternal life' as additional promised goods.
dismissed.note: καί is explanatory/continuative ('and so is the rest...'); English is a fair, readable rendering. Proposed 'rest from the kingdom' is wrong.
